- Dark brown/black discoloration at the tip
- Greenish mold patches in the middle section of the ear
- Mostly yellow/normal kernels elsewhere
- Bleached/dried husks

This is an ear (pod/seed) disease. Candidates: Aspergillus_Ear_Rot, Trichoderma_Ear_Rot, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Fusarium_Disease, Gibberella_Disease.

**Test image analysis:**
- Affected part: corn ear (pod/seed)
- Very dark brown/black at the **tip** of the ear
- Olive/greenish mold patches in the **middle** section of the ear
- Normal yellow kernels at the base/lower portion
- Bleached, dried husks peeled back

**Comparison to references:**

- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive-green to gray-green powdery mold starting at the tip. Reference seed_24 showed scattered green/olive patches on the ear — the closest visual match to the test image's middle-section mold. The dark tip is consistent with a heavy/dried Aspergillus infection at the tip (where infection originates), with lighter olive-green mold spreading toward the middle.
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Blue-green conidia from base to middle — green color partly matches, but Trichoderma spreads from the base upward, opposite to the tip-first pattern seen here.
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/red mold at tip — color does not match the dark brown/black tip.
- **Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight pod ref**: Dark mold at tip through husks — partly similar tip location, but SCLB mold is "gray-black felt-like" and there's no characteristic green middle-section mold.
- **Fusarium_Disease**: White/pink scattered patches — doesn't match.
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: White mycelium from base, or mummified brown ear — doesn't match.

**Conclusion**: The dark (heavily infected, possibly dried/aged) tip and olive-green scattered mold patches in the middle, with the infection progressing from the tip downward, best matches **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**.
